item.title: Atheist chat at the Whole Foods cafe on South Tunnel Road — Tue Oct 13, 10:00 AM
item.description:
Asheville Atheists Please come visit with us **Sunday Oct 18** to chat with like-minded people. Our new location is liked a lot.
We're meeting **once a month on Sunday mornings**. (After this, the next two will likely be **November 15 and Demember 11.)**
If you *think* you *might* come, please mark **Attend** below; that helps us know how many tables to put together. But many have come without marking that and that's fine.
Our great new location is **the cafe upstairs** at **Whole Foods, 4 South Tunnel Road (across from the mall).** They have coffee and a lot more. Maybe you have shopping you want to do at Whole Foods or one of the other businesses on Tunnel Road before or after the meeting.
**We start at 10am and end at noon**, but you're welcome to arrive or leave according to your own schedule.
If some folks want to have serious conversations about religion and/or atheism, while others just want to chat about other things, we'll use two sets of tables.
**We hope *you* stop by*

item.title: The Connect: Community Jam — Tue Oct 13, 8:00 PM — The One Stop
item.description:
Introducing The Connect: a weekly community jam at The One Stop curated by Women to the Front on Tuesdays, 8-11pm.
Asheville Music Hall The One Stop has a long history of being a place where musicians come together. The Connect is about continuing that spirit while helping create something new. This weekly jam aims to be a welcoming, respectful space where professional musicians, rising artists, and everyone in between can come together to collaborate, connect, and learn from each other.
Each week will feature a thoughtfully curated group of musicians who will start the night with a short set and then open the night to a jam. The goal is to build community across different generations, backgrounds, genres, and levels of experience. We are committed to creating an environment where everyone can feel safe, respected, and encouraged to attend.
Come play, come listen, come make some new friends, and help us reconnect with Asheville’s music community.
Source: LiveMusicAsheville.com

item.title: Ask About Our Featured Listings — Wed Oct 14 — LiveMusicAsheville.com
item.description:
Established in February 2019, LiveMusicAsheville.com now reaches thousands of people every week actively searching for live music in the Asheville area. Roughly 60% of our traffic comes from Google Search as we dominate the top of the results for queries such as “Asheville live music” & “live music Asheville”. Meanwhile our direct traffic is experiencing explosive growth, proving more locals are now using us as their go-to music calendar. Our free listings include just the basics of Who’s Playin’ Where & When. Our Featured Listings really stand out among the dozens of events on the calendar every day. While we update every Wednesday for the following Friday thru Thursday, these Featured Listings are published much sooner and include your picture or poster, a description of the event and the venue, website/ticket links and a Google map. We also share these events on our social media stories to help further promote your show.
Source: LiveMusicAsheville.com

item.title: Spaces Between…a witnessing, solo exhibition by Kristine Hunter — Thu Oct 22, 4:30 AM — Holden Arts Center
item.description:
Elizabeth Holden Gallery’s exhibition Spaces Between…a witnessing featuring the work of Kristine Hunter will be on view at Warren Wilson College from October 22nd to December 5th, 2026. The exhibition opening reception is on October 22nd from 4:30-6:00 PM. The Elizabeth Holden Gallery is open M-F, 10-4 pm and most Saturdays 1-4pm.
Artist Statement
From an early age, I was fascinated by human anatomy books, particularly their transparent pages that revealed the body layer by layer—skeleton, muscles, organs, each distinct yet inseparable from the whole. This early fascination with the visible and hidden layers of the body continues to shape my artistic practice.
My work explores identity, memory, belonging, and the continual process of constructing and deconstructing the self. I view our experiences as layers that accumulate within us, shaping who we become while remaining connected to what came before. item.title: Shut Up & Write - South Asheville — Sun Nov 1, 10:30 AM
item.description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina Coworking for writers in your area! Join us for some focused writing time. All writers and all experience levels are welcome and don’t worry, no one will see what you've written. This session is about getting your writing done and meeting other writers in your area.
Please arrive a few minutes early to say hello to everyone, grab a drink, and get your writing tools ready. Once everyone’s arrived, I will lead quick introductions and then set the timer for our quiet and focused writing session.
Afterward, we’ll have time to chat and get to know each other. We often talk about our successes and challenges as writers. If you don’t have time to stick around, no worries!
A note about the format We don’t host critiques or readings. These events are a safe space for writers of all skill levels and genres to work on their craft, so no one will read or critique your writing.
For our full event schedule, visit https://shutupwrite.com

Come join us on Tuesdays to joyfully protest the present authoritarian administration. Come with or without a sign, we have extras to share. On October 20, join us for a silent "Signs of Fascism" march at 4:45pm. The march will start at the corner of Fairfax and Haywood proceeding to the west Asheville Library where early voting is taking place. If anyone is not able to march the .7mi route, meet us on the sidewalk in front of the library. Park across the street at the parking lot and go the Bap
Source: Buncombe County Democratic Party

item.title: Come sing with us! Vocal workshop and rehearsal - Land Of The Sky Chorus — Tue Nov 3, 6:30 PM
item.description:
Asheville Area A Cappella Singers Whether you are an experienced singer, or just like to sing in your car, come join us as our guest! The Land of The Sky Chorus, located in Asheville, NC, is welcoming guests - men and women - who are interested in joining us in the world-wide community of a cappella singing.
No experience is required; we provide music, voice training and an enjoyable singing experience under expert leadership. Our repertoire of music is fun and spans many styles - most songs are easy to learn and sing. Learning materials are provided to help you get started, and you will be paired with a singing "Buddy" so you can join in right away.
We will be here to greet you as early as 6:15pm to help you get situated.
Source: Asheville Area A Cappella Singers

item.title: Dead Gowns / lamplight / JoJo Harnish — Fri Nov 6, 8:00 PM — Static Age Records
item.description:
As **Dead Gowns**, Maine songwriter Geneviève Beaudoin navigates between folk-rock, alt-country, and indie with a certain, weather-worn intimacy. On her second album, Vegas, she turns bright lights and dark waters into an exploration of quiet ruptures, blurred memories, and grief, guided by a voice that anchors even as it unfurls. w/ **lamplight -** Songwriting project of Ian Hatcher-Williams // Folk that comes creek-steeped \+ **JoJo Harnish -** blend of indie folk, traditional country, and Ame
Source: Static Age Records, Where Y'at AVL Music

item.description:

item.title: New Orthodox / Mike Johnson / Jed Willis — Thu Nov 12, 8:00 PM — Static Age Records
item.description:
**New Orthodox** (Hudson Valley, NY) - "The band's ethos leans heavily into minimalist repetition, sonic experimentation, and lyrical insights that give way to live performances and recordings that utilize space and silence to imitate the human experience. The music is both intimate and grand, charged and claustrophobic, taking the tools of country and spinning them out of context." w/ **Mike Johnson** and **Jed Willis** (Asheville) - pedal steel sets
Source: Static Age Records

item.title: Buncombe County Parks Update - Open and Closed Parks — Mon Dec 14
item.description: Email: parks@buncombecounty.orgPhone: (828) 250-4260Notice - Description: Information about Open and Closed ParksMany Buncombe County Parks were impacted by Hurricane Helene. While we are working diligently reopen parks as quickly as we can, some parks continue to remain closed. Please see the list below for which parks are open and which parks continue to be closed for safety reasons.OPEN Parks: Lake Julian Park (please note, some disc golf holes remain closed), Hominy Valley Park, Collier Cove Nature Preserve, North Buncombe Fields, Cane Creek Playground, Buncombe County Sports Park, Corcoran Paige River Park, Bent Creek River Park, Ledges Whitewater Park, and Hominy Creek River Park. If people choose to recreate on the river, we strongly encourage them to be aware of changes on streambanks and in the riverbed and the potential for unknown debris from Helene.CLOSED Parks: Charles D.
